correctness.rationale: Every coordinate secant slope of g is in [a,b] by absolute continuity, so Sg(x)-Sg(y)=diag(s)(x-y). For fixed increment h, convexity in each slope reduces the bound to masks with slopes in {a,b}. On edges of equal slope the contribution is at most m|hu-hv|; on cut edges it is <=m|hu-hv|+(b-a)|h_v|. A rooted path from r to v gives |h_v|<=|h_r|+sum_edges|grad h|=||h||_{G,r}, hence the upper modulus is m+(b-a)|cut|<=m+(b-a)maxcut. For the lower bound choose a maximum cut with coordinate base levels at differentiability points where slopes approach a,b, orient the root toward a derivative near absolute m, then add the same infinitesimal constant epsilon at every vertex. The input anchored norm is epsilon; the quotient approaches |g’(t_root)|+(b-a)maxcut. At a=b, g is affine and formula reduces to |a|; ReLU and absolute value have finite exact witnesses on strict affine regions. Graph family formulas follow from exact maxcut counts. The NP-hard reduction from general MAX-CUT to connected graphs uses bridging components and color-flip freedom. Independent three-vertex path ReLU pair attained exactly ratio 3, consistent with 1+maxcut=3.

value.rationale: The exact nonlinear Lipschitz modulus and its graph maxcut characterization show that pointwise nonexpansive nonlinearities may have unbounded two-input variation gain. It resolves an exact natural stability question in graph signal processing, supplies sharp family coefficients, and converts complexity of the operator modulus into classical graph combinatorics; this is more than a textbook composition theorem.

final_claim: For every finite connected unweighted simple graph G, anchor vertex r and globally Lipschitz real scalar g with essential derivative extremes a,b, the sharp two-input Lipschitz modulus of coordinatewise superposition in anchored graph variation is m+(b-a)maxcut(G), m=max(|a|,|b|). In particular ReLU gives 1+maxcut and absolute value 1+2maxcut, with NP-hard exact determination on arbitrary connected graphs.
